en.g: a male given name from Danish, equivalent to English Stephen

1001286.etyen:
Borrowed from Danish Steffen (“male given name”), a Danish form of Stefan (“male given name”), also found in Low German. Ultimately from Latin Stephanus (“male given name”), from Ancient Greek Στέφανος (Stéphanos, “male given name”), from Ancient Greek στέφανος (stéphanos, “wreath, crown”).
Compare German Steffen, Swedish Steffen and English Stephen.

weak verb of the e-class; especially in Nynorsk grammar, a weak verb taking -er (“-er”) in the present tense and normally a dental ending in the preterite and supine, such as kjøpe (“to buy”): kjøper, kjøpte, kjøpt
x: «Kjøpe» er et e-verb på nynorsk: «kjøper – kjøpte – har kjøpt».
“Kjøpe” is an e-verb in Nynorsk: “kjøper – kjøpte – har kjøpt”.
E-verb bøyes med -er i presens og -d(e) / -t(e) i preteritum og perfektum
E-verbs are conjugated with -er in the present and -d(e) / -t(e) in the preterite and perfect.

1004102.etyen:
Compound of e (“the letter e, referring to the present-tense ending -er”) + verb (“verb”), literally “e-verb”.
The first element refers to Nynorsk -er (“-er”), the characteristic present-tense ending of this verb class. The second element, verb (“verb”), is borrowed from Latin verbum (“word; verb”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *werh₁- (“to speak, say”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk e-verb (“e-verb”).

1004358.etyen: From rype (“grouse”) + falk (“falcon”), referring to the bird's diet.

en.g: a surname originating as a patronymic, originally meaning “son of Mons”

1004614.etyen:
From Mons (“male given name”) + -son (“patronymic suffix meaning “son of””), originally a patronymic meaning “son of Mons”. The given name Mons is a traditional Norwegian form of Magnus.
Compare Swedish Månsson (“patronymic surname”).

en.g: French West Africa; a former French colonial federation and general government in West Africa, ultimately comprising territories corresponding to present-day Senegal, Guinea, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Benin, Mali, Niger and Mauritania
x: Fransk Guinea var en av koloniene som inngikk i Fransk Vest-Afrika.
French Guinea was one of the colonies that formed part of French West Africa.
Fransk Vest-Afrika var fra 1904 til 1958 fransk generalguvernement i Vest-Afrika.
French West Africa was a French general government in West Africa from 1904 to 1958.

1004870.etyen:
Calque of French Afrique-Occidentale française (“French West Africa”), equivalent to fransk (“French”) + Vest-Afrika (“West Africa”).
The French colonial general government was first established in 1895 and was reorganized in 1902 and 1904. The latter reorganization established the administrative structure generally associated with Fransk Vest-Afrika.
Parallel formations include Norwegian Nynorsk Fransk Vest-Afrika, Danish Fransk Vestafrika, Swedish Franska Västafrika, German Französisch-Westafrika, Dutch Frans-West-Afrika and English French West Africa.

1005126.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂éd
Compound of G-dur (“G major”) + akkord (“chord”), literally “G-major chord”.
The first element G-dur (“G major”) contains the musical note name G (“G”) and dur (“major”). The latter is via German Dur (“major”) from Middle High German bēdūre (“B-natural; hard B”), from Medieval Latin b durum (“hard B”). The adjective is from Latin dūrus (“hard”), from Proto-Italic *dūros (“hard”), from Proto-Indo-European *dweh₂rós (“long, far”), from the root *dweh₂- (“far, long”).
The second element akkord (“chord”) is from French accord (“agreement; chord”), a deverbal derivative of French ac
